approach.method_basis: The Parent begins each objective with a recurrent SMILES policy copied from a frozen model trained on an unlabeled molecular corpus. It learns from the best-scoring half of each accepted batch together with the strongest eligible earlier elites from a memory of thirty-two molecules. Those historical records keep their original accepted strings and scores. Within history, an identity's weight decreases with the number of earlier fitting updates that used it, while the total current and historical coefficient shares stay fixed. The policy fits frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward with a weighted squared-error loss, taking up to twelve clipped Adam steps and retaining the last iterate. It then samples complete SMILES directly and fills the announced batch through chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection.
approach.novelty: Add a Huber residual loss whose transition scale is the starting weighted root-mean-square residual of that update. Large residuals then have capped influence before their sequence gradients combine; residuals inside the transition keep the Parent's exact squared-error expression. The threshold stays fixed throughout the update. This addresses concentration of fitting pressure that the inherited exposure counter does not measure. Earlier siblings changed training membership or views, normalized target probabilities, restored an earlier optimizer checkpoint, or projected a proposed step to protect historical loss. None bounded individual residual influence while retaining the Parent's current targets and exposure weights. The experiment will establish coefficient suppression and actual gradient-direction changes on identical policy states, then test whether subsequent useful discoveries improve.

hypothesis: Replace the Parent's exposure-weighted squared residual with an exposure-weighted Huber residual whose transition is the detached starting weighted root-mean-square residual of each update, floored at the square root of the inherited stopping tolerance and held fixed through that update, thereby capping individual residual influence while preserving selected members, augmented targets and exposure coefficients.

finding_summary.headline: Residual caps changed learning direction and improved AUC, but lowered final score and increased duplication
finding_summary.insights: Global gradient clipping did not make the row-level cap redundant: relative learning direction changed measurably in every prospective fitting opportunity. That establishes a real learning intervention, but more balanced residual influence did not provide the proposed final-score benefit. Faster discovery and the final endpoint separated: much of the AUC gain came from reaching strong DRD2 molecules earlier, where the parent already finished near the score ceiling, while sitagliptin lost substantial endpoint value. The molecular assessment found its stronger compact lactam–sulfonamide family in only one seed; broad core coverage in the other seeds did not supply equally useful structures. The cap also left target feasibility unresolved: historical exposures with positive, unattainable log-probability targets increased from 489 to 752 on the resulting trajectories. Starting caps affected current elites much more often than history, yet accepted-score averages and AUC increased, so the prediction of uniformly weaker early exploitation is not supported either. What remains open is how to preserve these early gains while reducing later repetition and avoiding the task-dependent loss of useful molecular families. The evidence does not isolate a particular suppressed row, token change or chemical feature as the cause of the endpoint loss.
finding_summary.results: The cap executed in all 450 updates. In the 420 historical updates followed by new proposals, it reduced influence on 1,465 of 4,200 selected row exposures at update start, including 1,092 current elites and 373 historical elites. The capped rows' mean share of absolute scalar influence fell from 69.22% to 59.37% on those same inputs. Every one of these updates changed the combined gradient direction even after global norm clipping, and every real first backward matched the Huber diagnostic exactly. Huber loss fell in 419 of the 420 updates, although 928 of 2,100 individual historical row exposures ended with larger residuals. All replicas completed. The three-seed final mean fell from 0.517655 to 0.508373, a paired change of -0.009283, with seed changes -0.026055, +0.032442 and -0.034235. The endpoint gain expected by the intent was not observed. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.406769 to 0.458439 and improved in every seed. The largest endpoint changes were a sitagliptin decrease of 0.080247 and a zaleplon increase of 0.035486. Raw duplicates rose from 36.22% to 48.80%, and batches needing additional sampling doubled from 29 to 58, while all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and novel.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal chemistry with concentrated peak families, unspecified stereochemistry and recurring nitroso chemistry in one seed.
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives are covered: the digest contains 900 accepted rows per task, including 870 optimizer proposals, and no tasks without trajectories. I read all child and Parent trajectory files. These are predominantly aromatic medicinal-chemistry structures with amides, sulfonamides, ethers, nitriles, heteroaromatics and saturated nitrogen rings. The digest's ring-closure rates span 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-token presence rates span 0.9448 to 0.9943; these indicate presence in strings, not fractions of aromatic atoms or measured three-dimensional shape. Every proposal pool has a stereocentre-marker rate of 0.0. Global connectivity diversity is substantial, while the highest-scoring subsets concentrate into particular series. The passive RDKit audit finds child Murcko-core counts of 414, 431, 403, 741 and 754 in task order, versus Parent counts of 472, 372, 537, 733 and 775. Those counts describe chemistry and do not establish utility or mechanism activation. Ordinary high-scoring amides, sulfonamides and cyclic amines appear synthetically plausible from connectivity, but the full output also includes excessive molecular growth, unresolved stereochemistry, unusual heteroatom states and recurrent N-nitroso linkages. No synthesis, stability, solubility, affinity or toxicity was measured here. All descriptor and substructure counts are passive readings of the supplied molecules, documented with exact input hashes and digest-to-trajectory checks in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-03-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json; its adjacent .audit.py reproduces the reading without candidate execution or objective calls. Scores below are recorded values, rounded for readability; associations are descriptive rather than proof of an objective's hidden chemical requirements.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is compact, largely planar aromatic amide chemistry. The best methoxy/cyanoquinoline bearing an N-methyl-N-pyridylmethyl carboxamide scores 0.532652 and has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic six-membered rings and molecular weight 332.363. Its benzyl and pyridyl positional analogues recur among the best molecules. Another strong family contains alkoxy- or ethyl-substituted quinoline carboxamides attached to a cyanophenyl group. These are recognizable amide, ether and nitrile combinations with plausible synthetic disconnections, although no route is supplied. The broad pool has median 24 heavy atoms and three rings. Compared with Parent n-3462511d7ff0, whose seed peaks include pyrrole carboxamides and linked aromatic amides, the child high end emphasizes fused cyanoquinolines; it retains the same broad aromatic-amide character. Child seed peaks are 0.467099, 0.532652 and 0.521093, so the new family is not the high-scoring chemistry in every seed.
liabilities: Large peptide-like, polyhydroxylated and long-chain excursions add substantial size and flexibility without the favorable compact arrangement; the cited zero-score polycycle has molecular weight about 866.1 and many unassigned potential stereocentres.

The high-scoring aromatic cores are relatively flat, and some alpha-substituted amide analogues introduce stereogenic connectivity without specifying configuration. These are chemical-quality limitations, not demonstrated causes of their scores.
missing_features: Lower-scoring proposals often fail to combine the compact azaaromatic scaffold, correctly placed nitrile and amide linkage seen together in the stronger series; individual aromatic rings or nitrogen atoms are already plentiful.

The best excerpt gives limited evidence for alternative fused-ring and amide-attachment arrangements outside its recurring quinoline families. It does not identify an unseen mandatory scaffold or establish that greater nitrogen content would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed span is 0 to 0.532652, with digest median 0.235877. Within a closely related pair, the cyanoquinoline N-methyl-pyridylmethyl amide scores 0.532652 versus 0.511984 without the nitrile. Moving the distal pyridine nitrogen gives 0.522408, while replacing that ring with phenyl still gives 0.531735: the exact arrangement matters more than simply adding nitrogen. In the ethyl/hydroxyquinoline family, the cyanophenyl carboxamide scores 0.512886 and the corresponding benzyl ketone scores 0.384734. Thus an amide connection and compact arrangement of aromatic/polar functions correlate with the better scores. The low examples include a highly oxygenated 61-heavy-atom structure at 0 and a long-chain ketoxime at 1.5745e-42. Ring count alone cannot explain this gradient, because ring-rich, heavily elaborated peptides and polycycles are also very poor.

per_task.generated_character: The digest's best molecules are all from seed 1 and share a fluorinated quinazoline connected through an O-methylene linker to a thiazole and a further azaaromatic ring. The best ethoxy analogue scores 0.616126, has 29 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings, no hydrogen-bond donors and molecular weight 418.4. Brominated, methoxy/ethoxy and aza-ring positional variants form a tight upper series. These ether and heteroaromatic connections look synthetically credible, although some densely substituted heteroarenes would require careful regioselectivity. Seed 2 instead ends in fluorinated diaryl-ether thioamides, including the cited 0.595362 final molecule. The full proposal pool has median 31 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings; halogen-token presence is 0.8621. Parent peaks emphasize other halogenated azaaryl/aniline and sulfonamide/imine arrangements. The child explores more distinct Murcko cores, 431 versus 372, while its highest excerpt still represents one recurring family.
liabilities: The full child trajectories contain 110 N-nitroso-amine substructure matches among 870 optimizer proposals, including 107 in seed 0; the Parent has five in total. This is a recurring functional-group liability requiring chemical review, rather than evidence from an assay of stability or toxicity. The seed-0 peak itself is an N-nitroso aniline at recorded score 0.589357.

The digest's final nitrogen-dioxide-like representation has an N-H centre and two singly bonded O-minus atoms with net charge minus one at score 0.576675. Another final molecule contains simultaneous sulfur-oxo and sulfur-thioxo bonds at 0.565662. These unusual states need structural and synthetic scrutiny despite accepted SMILES and nonzero scores.

Repeated halogenation and extended aromatic surfaces, together with thioamide-rich alternative series, make solubility, reactivity and physical form unresolved properties; the recorded objective does not measure them here.
missing_features: Weaker families often lack the coupled ether linker and multiple azaaromatic acceptor arrangements present in the best series, even when they already contain comparable aromatic surface and halogens.

Productive alternatives to the recurring quinazoline/thiazole/azaaryl connection are poorly represented in the highest excerpt. The observed alkoxy ties do not establish which new attachment geometry would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed span is 0.266174 to 0.616126, with digest median 0.563039. The lowest cited sulfone already has four aromatic rings and scores 0.266174; a halogenated benzothiazole/aniline structure scores 0.302799. Therefore abundant rings, halogens and aromatic surface are insufficient. The upper series associates higher scores with its particular azaaromatic and ether-linked arrangement. Methoxy and ethoxy versions of the same fluoropyridyl series both score 0.614046, showing that repeated terminal alkoxy changes need not add useful information. The small dichlorobenzonitrile and acyclic hydroxyurea-like example remain close to 0.50. This evidence supports whole-molecule connectivity and heteroatom placement, but cannot reveal an exact missing reference decoration.

per_task.generated_character: The upper molecules are aromatic-substituted saturated amines. The best series contains an azepane, a seven-membered nitrogen ring, joined to an alkylphenoxyethyl arm and a chlorophenethyl arm. Its best trichlorinated member scores 0.999996281, has 31 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings plus the azepane, molecular weight 482.923 and nine rotatable bonds. Another near-ceiling molecule is an aryl/benzyl-substituted diazepane bearing a methoxy group and a branched aminoalkyl substituent. These are conventional cyclic-amine, ether and aryl-alkyl connections, with plausible synthetic routes in principle, but their substituted saturated centres are not stereochemically specified. The Parent already supplies aromatic cyclic-amine families near the score ceiling. The child changes their ring and attachment choices rather than introducing ring-bound amine chemistry for the first time; its distinct Murcko cores number 403 versus the Parent's 537.
liabilities: The highest azepanes combine repeated chlorination, substantial aromatic/alkyl surface and flexible linkers. Their recorded score does not establish solubility, selectivity or a favorable conformational population.

The passive audit finds 605 of 870 child proposals with potential unassigned atom stereocentres, compared with 218 in the Parent, while the digest reports zero stereo markers. The chemical identities of those stereoisomers remain unresolved.
Late oversized polyamine and diaryl-chain variants add rotatable bonds and substituted centres; the cited 0.766099 example reaches molecular weight about 528.8 and fourteen rotatable bonds.
missing_features: Low-scoring examples often miss an unconjugated aliphatic amine presented in the appropriate aromatic and saturated-ring arrangement. Nitrogen in an amide or sulfonamide does not provide that same chemical feature.

The near-ceiling molecules establish no further missing binding feature. Their concrete representational omission is stereochemical specification: the best azepane contains two potential unassigned atom stereocentres, and the trajectory does not resolve configurations or poses.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed range is 3.80218e-05 to 0.999996281, with digest median 0.786939. The lowest cited acylated sulfonamide and nitro acylhydrazone have aromatic rings and nitrogen, but lack the unconjugated aliphatic amine arrangement characteristic of the highest series. In the passive audit, every one of the 217 molecules in the highest score quartile matches the stated amine structural proxy, and none contains an amide or sulfonamide. This is a connectivity association, not a pKa or binding-pose measurement. Within the leading azepanes, the dichlorinated example already scores 0.999996035, very close to the trichlorinated maximum. More chlorines are therefore not established as a useful general requirement. The final enlarged, flexible polyamine examples fall to 0.825120 and 0.766099, while a simpler diazepane analogue remains at 0.995455.

per_task.generated_character: This is a broad pool of ordinary aromatic heterocycles and polar linkers, with median 23 heavy atoms and three rings. The upper end repeatedly contains arylsulfonyl piperazines or diazepanes. The best is a bis-sulfonylated diazepane linking an ethoxy/methoxyphenyl group to a benzodioxole group: score 0.249068, 33 heavy atoms, molecular weight 498.579, two aromatic rings and four perceived rings overall. Both diazepane nitrogens are sulfonylated. The next example combines a thioamide, piperazine and arylsulfonyl benzodioxole at 0.242157. Smaller monoarylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazines also recur, such as the bromo/ethoxy compound at 0.223890. These are recognizable synthetic motifs, although the bis-sulfonyl and thioamide structures have substantial heteroatom and linker burdens. Parent high molecules already include arylsulfonyl piperazines and a bis-sulfonyl piperazine; the child substitutes different aromatic groups and, in its best molecule, expands the diaza ring. The global core counts, 741 versus 733, show that this pool is not structurally collapsed.
liabilities: The best bis-sulfonyl diazepane is acceptor-rich, has no hydrogen-bond donors and has seven rotatable bonds; ordinary-looking functional groups do not by themselves establish balanced physical properties.

The pool includes unnecessary long-chain growth, minimal solvent-like fragments and late nitro/dibromo or thiosemicarbazone structures. The cited thiosemicarbazone contains unresolved imine geometry, while heavy halogenation also appears in weak late proposals.
missing_features: Many weak proposals omit the integrated aromatic-sulfonamide-diazacycle arrangement, even when they contain isolated sulfur, nitrogen, halogens or aromatic rings.

The stronger molecules still provide only limited evidence about which linker orientation, diaza-ring geometry and aromatic attachment arrangement would improve beyond the observed modest scores. An exact unseen target combination cannot be inferred from this trajectory.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The recorded span is 0 to 0.249068, with digest median 0.124509. In the passive audit, 104 of 217 upper-quartile molecules contain a sulfonamide, versus four in the lower quartile. The zero-score imidic-acid fragment, long unsaturated nitrile/amine chain and carbon tetrachloride lack the aromatic/diaza-ring/sulfonyl combinations seen in the upper molecules. Conversely, the final dibromopyridyl sulfone has no sulfonamide-bound diaza ring and scores 0.078772. The initial polycyclic aromatic dicarbonyl molecule reaches 0.167839, showing that the recurring sulfonyl motif is an association rather than the only possible route to a nonzero score. Since the strongest diazepane has both nitrogens sulfonylated, this trajectory does not support a universal requirement for a free basic nitrogen.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring excerpt consists entirely of seed-1 dihydroquinolinone sulfonamides carrying benzyl or phenethyl groups, usually with a fluorophenyl terminus. The best para-fluorobenzyl compound scores 0.298922, has 23 heavy atoms, molecular weight 334.372, two aromatic rings and a fused partially saturated lactam ring. Its lactam and sulfonamide supply two donors and three acceptors. This is a compact, recognizable lactam/sulfonamide series with plausible synthetic disconnections. The full pool remains much broader, with median 24 heavy atoms, three rings and 754 distinct Murcko cores. Parent high examples occupy different guanidine, thioacyl/amide and acylsulfonamide families, including a fluorinated acylsulfonamide at 0.326097. Here the child seed maxima are 0.165623, 0.298922 and 0.156199: the compact lactam-sulfonamide family appears only in the stronger seed's upper excerpt, despite extensive ring chemistry elsewhere.
liabilities: Oversized fused/polycyclic, long-chain and polyfunctional excursions persist among very low scores; the cited zero-score complex ester has 60 heavy atoms and molecular weight about 837.1.

Stereochemically complex low-score polycycles and substituted late lactams omit configuration. The final multiacid/trifluoroacetamide structure also combines several polar groups and a bulky ring system without the successful compact linkage pattern.
missing_features: Most weak proposals lack the compact combination of a partially saturated lactam, sulfonamide linker and appropriately substituted benzyl group demonstrated by the stronger family; their isolated polar groups and rings do not reproduce it.

The trajectory gives no evidence for a required unseen pharmacophore beyond that local family. Its stronger nitrogens are lactam and sulfonamide nitrogens, and an obligatory free amine or particular stereoisomer cannot be inferred from the scores shown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest spans 0 to 0.298922 and has median 0.000001. Within the same lactam-sulfonamide arrangement, the benzyl analogue scores 0.271823, ortho-fluoro 0.282137, meta-fluoro 0.290771 and para-fluoro 0.298922. Extending the para-fluorobenzyl linker to phenethyl gives 0.280281. Thus this local gradient distinguishes terminal substitution and linker length. Moving the sulfonamide around the fused benzene gives effectively equal paired scores, so that change alone supplies no evidence of further progress. Huge polycycles and lipid-like elaborations score 0, while the final small methylaminomethylpyridine scores 2.53219e-11: neither molecular growth nor adding a free amine is sufficient. The final plausible aryl lactam/carboxamide at 0.000184 also shows that generic medicinal-chemistry appearance does not reproduce the successful functional-group combination.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal pool has digest stereocentre-marker rate 0.0. Passive graph perception finds 605 of 870 proposals with potential unassigned atom stereocentres in one pool, versus 218 for its Parent. The cited best substituted azepane has two potential unassigned atom centres. Complex low-score polycycles and simpler substituted amide/lactam examples show the same omission.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic connectivity without specifying stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs to preserve or deliberately explore stereochemical states when its existing connectivity creates stereocentres, and distinguish a specified compound from unresolved stereoisomers. Whether that affects utility must come from ordinary feedback; these trajectories do not establish a universally favorable configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A compact cyanoazaaryl amide at molecular weight 332.363 scores 0.532652 while a polyoxygenated structure near 866.1 scores 0. A compact lactam-sulfonamide near 334.4 scores 0.298922 while an elaborate ester near 837.1 scores 0. Very small fragments and unstructured long chains also score poorly. Conversely, a larger cyclic-amine molecule near 482.9 reaches a near-ceiling recorded score, so small size is not a universal answer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular extent is not consistently coupled to a coherent arrangement of functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generation should support complete, compact functional-group combinations and meaningful larger architectures without routinely drifting into fragment-sized endpoints or extended chains and polycycles. The chemical requirement is context-sensitive control of extent and connectivity, using available feedback rather than a universal molecular-size target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited near-ceiling azepanes and diazepanes contain unconjugated aliphatic amines, whereas a very low-scoring acylated sulfonamide contains nitrogen in strongly different bonding contexts. Elsewhere, a bis-sulfonylated diazepane is the strongest observed molecule despite both ring nitrogens being capped, and lactam/sulfonamide combinations lead another upper series. All these motifs already occur in the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: Nitrogen-rich output does not consistently retain the functional context that distinguishes free amines from resonance-deactivated nitrogen.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Chemical variation needs to preserve and explore nitrogen's neighboring atoms, conjugation, ring position and linker role as a connected motif. Generic nitrogen enrichment, universal amine addition or universal deprotection would discard the conflicting chemistry visible in the generator's own feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The recorded upper excerpts concentrate on cyanoazaaryl amides, linked azaaromatic ether systems, aromatic cyclic amines and lactam-sulfonamides. Some methoxy/ethoxy analogues tie at 0.614046, and paired sulfonamide positions on a fused lactam give effectively equal 0.298922 scores. These repeated decorations coexist with hundreds of distinct cores elsewhere and with weaker seeds that do not reproduce the stronger composite motif.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad global scaffold coverage coexists with limited productive exploration of attachment and linker alternatives around the strongest composite motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs ways to explore ring topology, attachment position and linker arrangement while retaining useful combinations already supported by its observations. Distinct strings, more peripheral substituents and larger global scaffold counts alone do not demonstrate this chemical capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One full proposal pool contains 110 N-nitroso-amine structural matches, with 107 in one seed, compared with five in the Parent. Digest examples also include an unusual N-H/two-O-minus arrangement at 0.576675 and simultaneous sulfur-oxo/sulfur-thioxo bonds at 0.565662. These are observable structures with recorded scores, not demonstrated stability, synthetic feasibility or toxicity results.
transferable_gaps.gap: Accepted molecular strings do not consistently retain conventional or well-supported heteroatom functional-group states.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs chemical-context handling that distinguishes conventional charge-separated groups and deliberately represented uncommon functions from incidental heteroatom rearrangements. Positive feedback and successful SMILES parsing should not be treated as evidence that every represented functional-group state is chemically suitable.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

activation_observables.measurement: Reconstruct unchanged selected targets, q_i and original accepted provenance. Recompute delta from the actual fixed training tensor's starting Parent weighted MSE and the inherited tolerance; verify that delta and q_i remain constant through all real steps. On every actual step compare the signed scalar MSE influence -2*q_i*r_i with -2*q_i*clip(r_i,-delta,delta). At resolved abs(r_i)>delta opportunities the absolute influence must decrease, while its sign stays the same; rows inside the quadratic region must retain the exact Parent row expression. For a capped set with nonzero uncapped influence, its share of total absolute scalar influence must decrease. Report counts, magnitudes and shares separately by current/history, positive target and residual sign with scalar tolerance 1e-8 + 1e-6*max(abs(actual),abs(reference)). These receipts establish influence clipping, not full-vector gradient dominance or target attainability. Target ceiling flags remain unchanged on fixed inputs.
activation_observables.name: Recompute every selected member's target from its unchanged accepted score and frozen-prior likelihood; record target attainability, target-minus-starting-likelihood sign and the specific target/weight/update change on fixed inputs.

activation_observables.measurement: At identical pre-update parameters on the same training tensor, measure actual Huber current/history group gradients, the combined gradient and the Parent exposure-weighted MSE comparator. Require a measurable direction change in at least one nonterminal residual-bearing clipping opportunity to support the proposed change in relative learning pressure; count every resolved, unresolved, scale-only and cancelled opportunity. Use full-vector differences and orthogonal components with tolerance 1e-8 + 1e-6*max(norms), and compare after the inherited global clipping rule as well as before it. Verify that the real first backward matches the Huber diagnostic and record actual first-step and complete-update parameter movement. A separately reduced group-gradient sum is diagnostic and may have floating-point discrepancies; direct first-backward agreement is the execution check. No diagnostic optimizer steps, random draws or mutation of gradient buffers are allowed.
activation_observables.name: Measure current-only, historical-only and actual combined gradients at identical pre-update parameters; for a weighting or update mechanism, verify changed gradient contributions and realized parameter updates without diagnostic optimizer steps.

Cancellation, Adam preconditioning and global clipping require same-state vector and real-backward checks. approach.method_basis: The Parent begins each objective with a recurrent SMILES policy copied from a frozen model trained on an unlabeled molecular corpus. It learns from the best-scoring half of each accepted batch together with the strongest eligible earlier elites from a memory of thirty-two molecules. Those historical records keep their original accepted strings and scores. Within history, an identity's weight decreases with the number of earlier fitting updates that used it, while the total current and historical coefficient shares stay fixed. The policy fits frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward with a weighted squared-error loss, taking up to twelve clipped Adam steps and retaining the last iterate. It then samples complete SMILES directly and fills the announced batch through chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection.
approach.novelty: Add a Huber residual loss whose transition scale is the starting weighted root-mean-square residual of that update. Large residuals then have capped influence before their sequence gradients combine; residuals inside the transition keep the Parent's exact squared-error expression. The threshold stays fixed throughout the update. This addresses concentration of fitting pressure that the inherited exposure counter does not measure. Earlier siblings changed training membership or views, normalized target probabilities, restored an earlier optimizer checkpoint, or projected a proposed step to protect historical loss. None bounded individual residual influence while retaining the Parent's current targets and exposure weights. The experiment will establish coefficient suppression and actual gradient-direction changes on identical policy states, then test whether subsequent useful discoveries improve.

finding_summary.headline: Residual caps changed learning direction and improved AUC, but lowered final score and increased duplication
finding_summary.insights: Global gradient clipping did not make the row-level cap redundant: relative learning direction changed measurably in every prospective fitting opportunity. That establishes a real learning intervention, but more balanced residual influence did not provide the proposed final-score benefit. Faster discovery and the final endpoint separated: much of the AUC gain came from reaching strong DRD2 molecules earlier, where the parent already finished near the score ceiling, while sitagliptin lost substantial endpoint value. The molecular assessment found its stronger compact lactam–sulfonamide family in only one seed; broad core coverage in the other seeds did not supply equally useful structures. The cap also left target feasibility unresolved: historical exposures with positive, unattainable log-probability targets increased from 489 to 752 on the resulting trajectories. Starting caps affected current elites much more often than history, yet accepted-score averages and AUC increased, so the prediction of uniformly weaker early exploitation is not supported either. What remains open is how to preserve these early gains while reducing later repetition and avoiding the task-dependent loss of useful molecular families. The evidence does not isolate a particular suppressed row, token change or chemical feature as the cause of the endpoint loss.
finding_summary.results: The cap executed in all 450 updates. In the 420 historical updates followed by new proposals, it reduced influence on 1,465 of 4,200 selected row exposures at update start, including 1,092 current elites and 373 historical elites. The capped rows' mean share of absolute scalar influence fell from 69.22% to 59.37% on those same inputs. Every one of these updates changed the combined gradient direction even after global norm clipping, and every real first backward matched the Huber diagnostic exactly. Huber loss fell in 419 of the 420 updates, although 928 of 2,100 individual historical row exposures ended with larger residuals. All replicas completed. The three-seed final mean fell from 0.517655 to 0.508373, a paired change of -0.009283, with seed changes -0.026055, +0.032442 and -0.034235. The endpoint gain expected by the intent was not observed. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.406769 to 0.458439 and improved in every seed. The largest endpoint changes were a sitagliptin decrease of 0.080247 and a zaleplon increase of 0.035486. Raw duplicates rose from 36.22% to 48.80%, and batches needing additional sampling doubled from 29 to 58, while all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and novel.

finding_summary.headline: Residual caps changed learning direction and improved AUC, but lowered final score and increased duplication
finding_summary.insights: Global gradient clipping did not make the row-level cap redundant: relative learning direction changed measurably in every prospective fitting opportunity. That establishes a real learning intervention, but more balanced residual influence did not provide the proposed final-score benefit. Faster discovery and the final endpoint separated: much of the AUC gain came from reaching strong DRD2 molecules earlier, where the parent already finished near the score ceiling, while sitagliptin lost substantial endpoint value. The molecular assessment found its stronger compact lactam–sulfonamide family in only one seed; broad core coverage in the other seeds did not supply equally useful structures. The cap also left target feasibility unresolved: historical exposures with positive, unattainable log-probability targets increased from 489 to 752 on the resulting trajectories. Starting caps affected current elites much more often than history, yet accepted-score averages and AUC increased, so the prediction of uniformly weaker early exploitation is not supported either. What remains open is how to preserve these early gains while reducing later repetition and avoiding the task-dependent loss of useful molecular families. The evidence does not isolate a particular suppressed row, token change or chemical feature as the cause of the endpoint loss.

finding_summary.headline: Residual caps changed learning direction and improved AUC, but lowered final score and increased duplication
finding_summary.insights: Global gradient clipping did not make the row-level cap redundant: relative learning direction changed measurably in every prospective fitting opportunity. That establishes a real learning intervention, but more balanced residual influence did not provide the proposed final-score benefit. Faster discovery and the final endpoint separated: much of the AUC gain came from reaching strong DRD2 molecules earlier, where the parent already finished near the score ceiling, while sitagliptin lost substantial endpoint value. The molecular assessment found its stronger compact lactam–sulfonamide family in only one seed; broad core coverage in the other seeds did not supply equally useful structures. The cap also left target feasibility unresolved: historical exposures with positive, unattainable log-probability targets increased from 489 to 752 on the resulting trajectories. Starting caps affected current elites much more often than history, yet accepted-score averages and AUC increased, so the prediction of uniformly weaker early exploitation is not supported either. What remains open is how to preserve these early gains while reducing later repetition and avoiding the task-dependent loss of useful molecular families. The evidence does not isolate a particular suppressed row, token change or chemical feature as the cause of the endpoint loss.
finding_summary.results: The cap executed in all 450 updates. In the 420 historical updates followed by new proposals, it reduced influence on 1,465 of 4,200 selected row exposures at update start, including 1,092 current elites and 373 historical elites. The capped rows' mean share of absolute scalar influence fell from 69.22% to 59.37% on those same inputs. Every one of these updates changed the combined gradient direction even after global norm clipping, and every real first backward matched the Huber diagnostic exactly. Huber loss fell in 419 of the 420 updates, although 928 of 2,100 individual historical row exposures ended with larger residuals. All replicas completed. The three-seed final mean fell from 0.517655 to 0.508373, a paired change of -0.009283, with seed changes -0.026055, +0.032442 and -0.034235. The endpoint gain expected by the intent was not observed. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.406769 to 0.458439 and improved in every seed. The largest endpoint changes were a sitagliptin decrease of 0.080247 and a zaleplon increase of 0.035486. Raw duplicates rose from 36.22% to 48.80%, and batches needing additional sampling doubled from 29 to 58, while all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and novel.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich medicinal chemistry with concentrated peak families, unspecified stereochemistry and recurring nitroso chemistry in one seed.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All five objectives are covered: the digest contains 900 accepted rows per task, including 870 optimizer proposals, and no tasks without trajectories. I read all child and Parent trajectory files. These are predominantly aromatic medicinal-chemistry structures with amides, sulfonamides, ethers, nitriles, heteroaromatics and saturated nitrogen rings. The digest's ring-closure rates span 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-token presence rates span 0.9448 to 0.9943; these indicate presence in strings, not fractions of aromatic atoms or measured three-dimensional shape. Every proposal pool has a stereocentre-marker rate of 0.0. Global connectivity diversity is substantial, while the highest-scoring subsets concentrate into particular series. The passive RDKit audit finds child Murcko-core counts of 414, 431, 403, 741 and 754 in task order, versus Parent counts of 472, 372, 537, 733 and 775. Those counts describe chemistry and do not establish utility or mechanism activation. Ordinary high-scoring amides, sulfonamides and cyclic amines appear synthetically plausible from connectivity, but the full output also includes excessive molecular growth, unresolved stereochemistry, unusual heteroatom states and recurrent N-nitroso linkages. No synthesis, stability, solubility, affinity or toxicity was measured here. All descriptor and substructure counts are passive readings of the supplied molecules, documented with exact input hashes and digest-to-trajectory checks in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-03-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json; its adjacent .audit.py reproduces the reading without candidate execution or objective calls. Scores below are recorded values, rounded for readability; associations are descriptive rather than proof of an objective's hidden chemical requirements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal pool has digest stereocentre-marker rate 0.0. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic connectivity without specifying stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs to preserve or deliberately explore stereochemical states when its existing connectivity creates stereocentres, and distinguish a specified compound from unresolved stereoisomers. Whether that affects utility must come from ordinary feedback; these trajectories do not establish a universally favorable configuration.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Chemical variation needs to preserve and explore nitrogen's neighboring atoms, conjugation, ring position and linker role as a connected motif. Generic nitrogen enrichment, universal amine addition or universal deprotection would discard the conflicting chemistry visible in the generator's own feedback.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs ways to explore ring topology, attachment position and linker arrangement while retaining useful combinations already supported by its observations. Distinct strings, more peripheral substituents and larger global scaffold counts alone do not demonstrate this chemical capability.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs chemical-context handling that distinguishes conventional charge-separated groups and deliberately represented uncommon functions from incidental heteroatom rearrangements. Positive feedback and successful SMILES parsing should not be treated as evidence that every represented functional-group state is chemically suitable.

applicability_conditions: This experiment applies to the supplied exposure-weighted Parent with accepted original-string replay and fixed augmented targets. The passive numerical audit reads its complete logs and scalar receipts only; it does not reconstruct historical parameter vectors, counterfactual gradients or molecules.

The RMS transition is calibrated once from the actual selected current/history tensor at update start and is detached. The inherited stopping threshold only supplies a numerical floor. It is not selected from task identity, held-out labels, future feedback or evaluation settings.

Huber fitting changes residual curvature and influence, not target feasibility. Positive log-probability targets remain unattainable, and jointly infeasible negative targets can remain. The cap preserves each instantaneous row's desired likelihood direction on fixed inputs but does not guarantee finite policy moves in that direction under shared parameters and Adam momentum.

The Parent's exposure coefficients and their current/history sums remain exact. Their interpretation is coefficients multiplying row losses; neither the actual group loss values nor group gradient shares must remain unchanged when the row loss becomes Huber. Exposure-count controls continue to validate weighting but do not exempt initialization or equal-count batches from Huber activation.

Large residuals can be valuable new reward information rather than noise. In the Parent fixed stream, most capped rows are current elites. Reducing their influence may further weaken early exploitation or worsen AUC, even if extreme residual concentration declines. There is no guarantee of improved chemistry, novelty or scores from a robust fitting statistic.

A scalar residual coefficient does not determine the norm or direction of its full sequence-parameter gradient. Cancellation, Adam preconditioning and global clipping require same-state vector and real-backward checks. Floating-point differences between train/eval execution or the larger legacy diagnostic tensor must be separated from changes in targets or the immutable delta source.

approach.method_basis: The Parent begins each objective with a recurrent SMILES policy copied from a frozen model trained on an unlabeled molecular corpus. It learns from the best-scoring half of each accepted batch together with the strongest eligible earlier elites from a memory of thirty-two molecules. Those historical records keep their original accepted strings and scores. Within history, an identity's weight decreases with the number of earlier fitting updates that used it, while the total current and historical coefficient shares stay fixed. The policy fits frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward with a weighted squared-error loss, taking up to twelve clipped Adam steps and retaining the last iterate. It then samples complete SMILES directly and fills the announced batch through chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection.
approach.novelty: Add a Huber residual loss whose transition scale is the starting weighted root-mean-square residual of that update. Large residuals then have capped influence before their sequence gradients combine; residuals inside the transition keep the Parent's exact squared-error expression. The threshold stays fixed throughout the update. This addresses concentration of fitting pressure that the inherited exposure counter does not measure. Earlier siblings changed training membership or views, normalized target probabilities, restored an earlier optimizer checkpoint, or projected a proposed step to protect historical loss. None bounded individual residual influence while retaining the Parent's current targets and exposure weights. The experiment will establish coefficient suppression and actual gradient-direction changes on identical policy states, then test whether subsequent useful discoveries improve.

research_intent.falsifier: The bound mechanism is refuted if delta cannot be reconstructed from the starting Parent weighted MSE and inherited floor, changes within an update, or supplies a gradient; if the actual loss or signed scalar derivative does not follow the registered piecewise rule; or if q_i, targets, membership or accepted original-sequence provenance changes. At numerically resolved capped-row opportunities, failure to reduce absolute scalar influence refutes the influence cap. A real first backward following the MSE comparator instead of the Huber objective also refutes implementation. If caps execute but every eligible nonterminal combined-gradient difference is below resolution or scale-only after global clipping, the stronger hypothesis that bounded row influence changes relative online learning is unsupported; scalar activation alone cannot confirm it. No clipping opportunities leave activation untested. Lost Parent code-path equivalence inside the quadratic region, diagnostic optimizer steps, or added RNG draws violate the bound controls. A missing complete paired score benefit rejects the proposed utility despite confirmed loss and gradient activation; larger MSE or individual historical worsening alone does not show failure to execute Huber fitting.

research_intent.mechanism: Replace the Parent's exposure-weighted squared residual with an exposure-weighted Huber residual whose transition is the detached starting weighted root-mean-square residual of each update, floored at the square root of the inherited stopping tolerance and held fixed through that update, thereby capping individual residual influence while preserving selected members, augmented targets and exposure coefficients.
